industry.headline: Meta reaches ~$17.1B settlement with 51 states, agrees to teen-safety limits including two-hour daily cap on Instagram/Facebook
industry.summary: Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1B and adopt sweeping teen-safety design changes across Instagram and Facebook, resolving a 2023 multistate lawsuit alleging it knowingly targeted underage users to maximize engagement. Terms (pending court approval) include a default two-hour daily time limit cumulative across both apps and multiple accounts, liftable only by a parent, plus removal of engagement-driving features like like-counts — the largest tech settlement of its kind and a direct validation of NOMO's screen-time-reduction value proposition just as US GTM ramps.

industry.headline: EFF: Meta's settlement structure financially pressures TikTok, YouTube, and Snap into matching teen restrictions
industry.summary: EFF's analysis of the Meta settlement notes it includes over $11B in state payments over 10 years plus an additional $5B contingent on competitors adopting equivalent age-assurance and teen-restriction measures — effectively giving states a financial incentive to push industry-wide adoption of screen-time caps and notification blackouts, which would shift the whole industry baseline toward the kind of built-in limits NOMO's positive-incentive layer complements.

industry.headline: TikTok's 'Unusual' Kids Privacy Settlement Sidelines FTC Role
industry.summary: The DOJ, not the FTC, closed the government's six-year COPPA case against TikTok via a $400M settlement — an unusual departure from the FTC's traditional role that raises questions about whether remedies match the rigor of a full-user-journey consent decree. Signals intensifying scrutiny of youth data handling (age verification, parental consent, retention) that NOMO's school and brand partners will expect to see addressed in any student-facing rewards/leaderboard features.
